source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1–2, introduction; p. 5, Theorem 2.2; p. 6, Theorem 3.1; pp. 20–22, proof of Theorem 2.2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper treats fixed binary potential outcomes under unrestricted design-estimator procedures, reduces the two-arm problem to a scalar binomial experiment, and proves an n^{-1}-C_A n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}) expansion attained by balanced Bernoulli randomization and nonlinear shrinkage.

Theorem 1 optimizes bounded two-arm ATE risk over all measurable estimators and gives the finite reduced minimax characterization; footnote 10 states its characterization coincides with Sudijono et al.'s two-arm result.

Theorem 2.1 proves complete randomization under permutation invariance for a fixed assignment vector and invariant estimator; Theorem 3.1 gives a reduced optimization over linear estimation schemes; Theorem 3.2 gives the two-arm Neyman-allocation/difference-in-means specialization.
The paper studies design-unbiased estimation of bounded finite-population totals and derives sharp finite minimax results with pairwise-independent sampling; its scope retains unbiasedness.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a worked four-arm response-tube prior instance for the mixed-sign contrast, including its finite spline weights and at least one missing-active-arm count face; this makes the all-face construction auditable before the general proof.

Add an explicit literature-location sentence establishing that the two-arm Airy papers formulate only a binary treatment/control experiment and do not address multi-arm contrasts; this will make the strict-extension positioning immediately checkable.
State a finite-horizon corollary translating the certified risk-bracket tolerance into an allocation decision rule for a prespecified four-regimen contrast.

recommended_next_step: Advance this angle to Stage 0, beginning with the all-count response-tube Bayes inequality and a concrete four-arm tube exhibit.
